    1985 to 2016" file); the original read a local copy of the same file.
  - The pre-processing (drop HDI, exclude 2016, drop country-year) is the
    same as in the report. The exploration and R logistic models that follow
    are the original analysis, kept as written.

Pre-loading the data and pre-processing any missing values

```{r}
library(tidyverse) # general
library(ggalt) # dumbbell plots
library(countrycode) # continent
library(rworldmap) # quick country-level heat maps
library(gridExtra) # plots
library(broom) # significant trends within countries

## Loading dataset
suicidedata <- read.csv("../data/master.csv")

## Summary statistics 
Hmisc::describe(suicidedata)

## Too many missing values to draw any conclusions
## Removing from dataset
library(dplyr)
suicidedata <- suicidedata %>% 
  select(-c(HDI.for.year)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

## Processing data as nominal factors 
data_nominal <- c('country', 'sex', 'continent')
suicidedata[data_nominal] <- lapply(suicidedata[data_nominal], function(x){factor(x)})

# Making age ordinal
## suicidedata$age <- factor(suicidedata$age, ordered = T, levels = c("5-14", "15-24", "25-34", "35-54", "55-74", "75+"))


library(dplyr)
suicidedata <- suicidedata %>%
  filter(year != 2016) %>% # I therefore exclude 2016 data
  select(-country.year)
```

##### Testing numerical variables for normality

Determining the distribution of suicide count. 

```{r}
## Plotting values 
x <- suicidedata$suicides_no
h<-hist(x, 
 breaks=12,
 col="blue",
 xlab="Suicide Counts",
 main="Distribution of Suicie Counts Globally")

xfit<-seq(min(x), max(x), length=40)
yfit<-dnorm(xfit, mean=mean(x), sd=sd(x))
yfit <- yfit*diff(h$mids[1:2])*length(x)
lines(xfit, yfit, col="red", lwd=2)
box()

## Removing outliers and re-plotting
Q <- quantile(suicidedata$suicides_no, probs=c(.25, .75), na.rm = FALSE)
iqr <- IQR(suicidedata$suicides_no)
up <-  Q[2]+1.5*iqr # Upper Range  
low<- Q[1]-1.5*iqr # Lower Range

suicidecountoutliers <- subset(suicidedata, suicidedata$suicides_no > (Q[1] - 1.5*iqr) & suicidedata$suicides_no  < (Q[2]+1.5*iqr))

x <- suicidecountoutliers$suicides_no
h<-hist(x, 
 breaks=12,
 col="blue",
 xlab="Pressure",
 main="Pressure Distribution")

xfit<-seq(min(x), max(x), length=40)
yfit<-dnorm(xfit, mean=mean(x), sd=sd(x))
yfit <- yfit*diff(h$mids[1:2])*length(x)
lines(xfit, yfit, col="red", lwd=2)
box()

#skewness and kurtosis from semTools with standard error 
tpskew<-semTools::skew(suicidedata$suicides_no)
tpkurt<-semTools::kurtosis(suicidedata$suicides_no)
#We divide the skew statistic by the standard error to get the standardised score
tpskew[1]/tpskew[2]
tpkurt[1]/tpkurt[2]

```

### Differences - Non-Parametric Tests

Mann Whitney U Test

Using Mann Whitney U test we found there was a stat significant for gender and suicide

W = 53248014, p-value < 2.2e-16

```{r}
psych::describeBy(suicidedata$suicides.100k.pop,group=suicidedata$sex)

#Create data subsets for each sex
femaledata <- subset(suicidedata, sex=="female")
maledata <-subset(suicidedata, sex=='male')

#Create plots of these
gs <- ggplot(femaledata, aes(x=suicides.100k.pop))
gs <- gs + labs(x="Female")
gs <- gs + geom_histogram(binwidth=2, colour="black", aes(y=..density.., fill=..count..))
gs <- gs + scale_fill_gradient("Count", low="#DCDCDC", high="#7C7C7C")
gs <- gs + stat_function(fun=dnorm, color="red",args=list(mean=mean(femaledata$suicides.100k.pop, na.rm=TRUE), sd=sd(femaledata$suicides.100k.pop, na.rm=TRUE)))
gs

gs <- ggplot(maledata, aes(x=suicides.100k.pop))
gs <- gs + labs(x="Male")
gs <- gs + geom_histogram(binwidth=2, colour="black", aes(y=..density.., fill=..count..))
gs <- gs + scale_fill_gradient("Count", low="#DCDCDC", high="#7C7C7C")
gs <- gs + stat_function(fun=dnorm, color="red",args=list(mean=mean(maledata$suicides.100k.pop, na.rm=TRUE), sd=sd(maledata$suicides.100k.pop, na.rm=TRUE)))
gs

# Test for differences in gender
stats::wilcox.test(suicides.100k.pop~sex, data=suicidedata) 
```

Using the Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared test we found there was a stat sig for age and suicide

Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 7008.9, df = 5, p-value < 2.2e-16

One Way Anova (lecture 06_Difference_II). F = 909.79, p <.001
[F(5, 27814) = 909.79, p = <.001]. 

All age groups have a statistical significance on suicide. 

```{r}
## Stats
psych::describeBy(suicidedata$suicides.100k.pop,group=suicidedata$age)

# Test for differences in age
stats::kruskal.test(suicides.100k.pop~age, data=suicidedata) 

## One Way ANOVA 
library(userfriendlyscience)
library(ppcor)
library(olsrr)
one.way <- oneway(suicidedata$age , y = suicidedata$suicides.100k.pop , posthoc = 'Tukey')
one.way

```

#### Testing for correlations for non-parametric variables

All our variables are non-normally distributed so we will use Spearman.

Correlation between suicide rate per 100k and GDP per capita.  p-value < 2.2e-16 and  rho = 0.07306332.

Correlation betweensuicide rate per 100k and population size. S = 2.8166e+12, p-value < 2.2e-16 and  rho = 0.2151278.

```{r}
cor.test(suicidedata$suicides.100k.pop, suicidedata$gdp_per_capita...., method = "spearman")

cor.test(suicidedata$suicides.100k.pop, suicidedata$population, method = "spearman")

```

#### Building Log Model 1

Model baseline

The Chi-square stat is 6370, df = 1, which is statiscally signficant (p < 0.001)

Deviance Residuals: 
    Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max  
-1.5707  -1.0446   0.4148   0.9327   4.6959  

AIC: 32200

```{r}
library("car")
library("stargazer")



suicidedata$sex = recode(suicidedata$sex,"'female' = 1; 'male' = 0")

logmodel1 <- lm(suicides.100k.pop ~ sex, data=suicidedata, na.action=na.exclude, family=binomial())
logmodel1

lmtest::lrtest(logmodel1)
summary(logmodel1)
stargazer(logmodel1, type="text")
```
Testing linear
```{r}

library("car")
library("stargazer")

suicidedata$sex = recode(suicidedata$sex,"'female' = 1; 'male' = 0")

lmodel1 = lm(suicidedata$suicides.100k.pop~suicidedata$sex)
stargazer(lmodel1 , type="text")

#Check assumptions
#Cooks distance
cooks.distance(lmodel1)
#Plot Cooks distance
plot(cooks.distance(lmodel1), ylab="Cook's statistic")

#Create histogram
#A density plot of the residuals
plot(density(resid(lmodel1))) 

#Create a QQ plotqqPlot(model, main="QQ Plot") #qq plot for studentized resid 
leveragePlots(lmodel1) # leverage plots

## The mean of residuals is zero
mean(lmodel1$residuals)

plot(lmodel1)

## The variability in X values is positive
var(suicidedata$suicides.100k.pop)  

## The X variables and residuals are uncorrelated
cor.test(suicidedata$suicides.100k.pop, lmodel1$residuals)

#Collinearity
vifmodel<-vif(lmodel1)
#Calculate tolerance
1/vifmodel

```

```{r}
lmodel1a <- lm(suicides.100k.pop ~ sex, data=suicidedata[-c(1259, 22281, 24333,20543,11377,20531,13689), ])
gvlma::gvlma(lmodel1a)
plot(lmodel1a)
```




Check later ofr LG
```{r}
## Zone in on Chi for the model to check for improvement
modelChi <- logmodel1$null.deviance - logmodel1$deviance
modelChi

## Zone in on Degrees of freedom for our model (will usually be 1)
chidf <- logmodel1$df.null - logmodel1$df.residual
chidf

## Zone in on Chi for getting the probability or no model pr baseline
chisq.prob <- 1 - pchisq(modelChi, chidf)
chisq.prob

## Test for pseudo R2 and chi square.
## R Squared is tiny
rcompanion::nagelkerke(logmodel1, restrictNobs = T)

## Exponential coefficients.
## Factor % 
exp(coefficients(logmodel1))

## Plot a ROC curve and look for specificity and sensitivity.
## We want to look at the Area under the curve
## .5 is weak, .8 is strong
Epi::ROC(form=suicidedata$sex ~ suicidedata$suicides.100k.pop, plot="ROC")
```

#### Building Model 2

Adding in age

The Chi-square stat is 7911.87, df = 6, which is statistically significant (p < 0.001)

Cox and Snell R2 and Nagelkerke R2 are pseudo R2 statistics - in this case they indicate that between 20% and 33% of the variance is explained by age.


```{r}
library("car")
library("stargazer")

logmodel2 <- glm(sex ~ suicides.100k.pop + age, data=suicidedata, na.action=na.exclude, family=binomial())
logmodel2

lmtest::lrtest(logmodel2)
summary(logmodel2)
stargazer(logmodel2, type="text")
```


```{r}
## Zone in on Chi for the model to check for improvement
modelChi <- logmodel2$null.deviance - logmodel2$deviance
modelChi

## Zone in on Degrees of freedom for our model (will usually be 1)
chidf <- logmodel2$df.null - logmodel2$df.residual
chidf

## Zone in on Chi for getting the probability or no model pr baseline
chisq.prob <- 1 - pchisq(modelChi, chidf)
chisq.prob
```

```{r}
## Test for pseudo R2 and chi square.
## R Squared is tiny
rcompanion::nagelkerke(logmodel2, restrictNobs = T)

## Exponential coefficients.
## Factor % 
exp(coefficients(logmodel2))

#Collinearity
vifmodel2 <- vif(logmodel2)
1/vifmodel2 
sqrt(vif(logmodel2)) 
```
